findings.statement: No single authoritative capability catalog joins identity, maturity, entry publication, scene usage and product usage.
The 63-key runtime capability registry diverges from the CAP-01 39-key candidate catalog and re-includes 24 excluded page identities.
Eight acceptance contracts exist, but none of their capability keys are present in the runtime sc.capability catalog and no current evidence bundle exists in the checkout.
Released product snapshots expose 274 entry compatibility aliases as released while omitting capability_maturity; these aliases must not be counted as business capabilities.
All 17 business scenarios are treated as product_released when any member menu is released; capability maturity and complete scene evidence are not part of that decision.
Capability and release authoring are still platform-admin-only; capability operator, scene operator and release reviewer duties are not implemented as separate authorities.

history_reconciliation.conclusion: The current 63-key runtime UI capability registry is not a migration of the CAP-01 39-key candidate catalog. It re-includes 24 explicitly excluded page/entry identities and retains project.initiation.enter instead of canonical project.initiation.create.

limitations: This audit is read-only and did not generate or validate new maturity evidence bundles.
Native entry counts are operational scope indicators, not business capability counts.
Daily sc_demo is a single-tenant observation and not proof for all environments.
The 57 visible runtime registry rows reflect wutao in sc_demo and must not be generalized to all roles.
